newsitem.title: KENYA: Maize arrivals at Mombasa port detailed.
newsitem.headline: Maize arrivals at Mombasa port detailed.

text.p: A consignment of 47,856 tonnes of maize has arrived at the port of Mombasa while a further 25,430 tonnes are expected soon, shipping sources said on Friday.
They said part of the maize was to fill a government tender to feed drought victims and part was brought in by private business.
They would not give exact quantities.
Last week, a consignment of 23,000 tonnes brought in by Cargill Kenya from Houston in the U.S. without pre-shipment inspection was rejected by the National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB).
Cargill said the maize was fit for human consumption but the board said correct procedures had not been followed before it was shipped into the country.
Over the next two weeks 46 ships carrying a total of 129,435 tonnes of assorted cargo were expected to dock in Mombasa, according to a weekly shipping report.
The cargo includes maize, wheat, fertiliser, clinker, 836 vehicles, sugar and beans.

Four ships were waiting off the port, including the Constathea, which arrived on April 7 with 20,000 tonnes of maize, and the An Nooru, which arrived Thursday with 15,500 tonnes of wheat from Argentina.
